Judgment on Board 07.04.2026
1.

The appellant/insurance company has preferred this appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 calling in question the legality, validity and correctness of the impugned award dated 23.11.2019 passed by Sixth Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ambikapur, District Sarguja, in Claim Case No.52/2019 by which the claim application of the claimants is allowed and liability has been fastened upon the insurance company to pay the amount of compensation.

entities.text: Sixth Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ambikapur, District Sarguja
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Learned counsel appearing for the appellant/insurance company, would submit that the deceased was also contributory negligent in driving the vehicle, as it is a case of head-on collision, therefore,
50% amount of compensation ought to have been deducted towards the contributory negligent of the deceased and the appeal be allowed.
3. Learned counsels appearing for the respondents would support the impugned award and submit that the appeal of the insurance company is liable to be dismissed.
4. I have heard learned counsel appearing for the parties, considered their rival submissions made herein-above and went through the records with utmost circumspection.

5. The appellant/insurance company had filed return before the Claims Tribunal and has taken an alternative plea in para 28(e) that if the Court comes to the conclusion that the accident has occurred then it is a case of head-on collision, therefore, the driver, owner & insurance company of Divisional Manager, United India ... vs Smt. Nayantara Bhagat on 7 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112199292/
2 both the vehicle should be liable towards the contributory negligence, but surprising no witness has been examined on behalf of the insurance company except the statement of Anup Mehta,
Investigator, who has investigated the matter to prove the fact of contributory negligence.

As such,
there is no evidence on record that the deceased was also contributory negligent in driving the offending vehicle.
Therefore, I do not find any merit in this appeal, the same deserves to be and accordingly dismissed.

Sd/-
 (Sanjay K. Agrawal)
